terms.name: Accessibility grouping
terms.definition: Collapsing a cluster of elements, an icon plus a label plus a value, into one thing assistive technology stops at, instead of three stops that mean nothing apart.

terms.name: Afrofuturism
terms.definition: A style that pictures technology through the African diaspora, combining cosmic imagery, textile and mask pattern, gold and indigo, and geometric ornament used structurally.

terms.name: Aqua
terms.definition: Apple's early Mac OS X look of glossy blue gel buttons, pinstripes, gumdrop window controls, and a pulsing default button.

terms.name: Avatar
terms.definition: A small image standing in for a person or entity, falling back to initials or a generic glyph when there is no picture.

terms.name: Box
terms.definition: A bordered container, optionally titled, that groups logically related controls so the grouping is drawn rather than implied by spacing alone.

terms.name: Callout
terms.definition: A boxed note set into the flow of content to carry a warning, tip or aside, coloured by severity and staying put once shown.

terms.name: Chart annotation
terms.definition: A note pinned onto the data itself: a callout, arrow, or highlighted span that tells the reader what to see in the chart.

terms.name: CMYK
terms.definition: The subtractive print colour model: cyan, magenta and yellow inks plus a key black, mixing by absorbing light, with a gamut narrower than any screen's.

terms.name: Color temperature
terms.definition: Whether a colour reads warm (toward red and orange) or cool (toward blue), the axis designers use to bias a neutral grey without changing its lightness.

terms.name: Compound grid
terms.definition: Two or more grids of different column counts overlaid in one layout, so a page can carry several rhythms while still sharing one structure.

terms.name: Contextual alternates
terms.definition: Substitute letterforms a font swaps in automatically based on the neighbouring characters, so joins and repeats look natural.

terms.name: Cyberpunk UI
terms.definition: A dystopian sci-fi interface style: near-black surfaces, one or two toxic neon accents, monospace all-caps labels, clipped corners, and scanline or glitch noise laid over the top.

terms.name: Density
terms.definition: How much content a system packs into a given area, tuned as a named setting so the same components can run comfortable or compact.

terms.name: Dissolve
terms.definition: A fade that carries the eye from one image or state to another without any movement, inherited from film editing vocabulary.

terms.name: Drawer
terms.definition: A panel docked to one edge of the screen that slides in over the content, holding navigation or the details of the thing you selected.

terms.name: Editorial web design
terms.definition: A style that borrows print magazine craft for the screen: a visible column grid, display type at poster scale, pull quotes, rules, and captioned images set into the text.

terms.name: Exit animation
terms.definition: The motion an element plays on its way out, which requires deferring its removal from the layout until the animation has finished.

terms.name: Feature gate
terms.definition: Showing a locked feature in place, with its real position in the interface, so the reader sees what upgrading would unlock rather than a hidden absence.

terms.name: Flashing content
terms.definition: Content that flashes more than three times per second in a large enough area, restricted because it can trigger seizures.

terms.name: Focus order
terms.definition: The sequence keyboard focus follows through a page, which should match reading order instead of source quirks or positive tabindex values.

terms.name: Forgiving format
terms.definition: Accepting whatever shape the reader types and normalising it afterwards, instead of rejecting input that differs only in spacing or punctuation.

terms.name: Gloss
terms.definition: A wet plastic finish made from a light gradient across the top half of a control, a highlight arc, and a darker lower half.

terms.name: Halftone
terms.definition: Rendering tone as a grid of dots that vary in size, borrowed from print and used to give flat interface art a comic or newsprint feel.

terms.name: Hit slop
terms.definition: Invisible padding that extends a control's activatable area beyond its drawn bounds, so a small icon can stay small and still be easy to hit.

terms.name: Hyphenation ladder
terms.definition: Three or more consecutive lines ending in a hyphen, which builds a visible staircase down the right edge of a column.

terms.name: Inline validation
terms.definition: Checking a field as the reader fills or leaves it and showing the verdict beside that field, rather than saving every complaint for the submit button.

terms.name: Jank
terms.definition: Visible stutter in motion caused by frames arriving late or not at all, so an animation that should be continuous reads as juddering.

terms.name: Knob
terms.definition: A round control turned by dragging in an arc, borrowed from hardware and mostly found in audio and creative tools.

terms.name: Legibility
terms.definition: How easily one letter can be told apart from another, a property of the typeface's drawing rather than of how the text is set.

terms.name: Listbox
terms.definition: An always visible list of options you choose from with the keyboard or pointer, without a popup or a text field.

terms.name: Marking menu
terms.definition: A radial menu that can be answered before it appears: waiting shows the menu, while a confident stroke in the item's direction selects it outright.

terms.name: Metered paywall
terms.definition: A paywall that grants a fixed number of free items per period and counts down publicly, so the barrier arrives only after the reader is invested.

terms.name: Modifier key
terms.definition: A key held to change what another input means, so the same click or keystroke can copy instead of move, or add instead of replace.

terms.name: Multimodal interface
terms.definition: An interface that accepts and answers in more than one channel at once, letting a person speak, type, touch, or point and pick whichever suits the moment.

terms.name: Node port
terms.definition: The typed stub on a node where a wire may land, coloured or shaped by what it accepts, so a connection that would make no sense refuses to complete.

terms.name: OpenType features
terms.definition: Optional glyph substitutions and spacing rules packed inside a font file, addressed by four-letter tags and switched on from CSS.

terms.name: Overshoot
terms.definition: The part of a motion that carries past its final value before coming back, the visual signature of an underdamped spring or a back easing curve.

terms.name: Password reveal toggle
terms.definition: The control inside a password field, usually an eye or the word Show, that switches the characters between masked and readable.

terms.name: Pointer capture
terms.definition: Redirecting all events for one pointer to a chosen element, so a drag keeps reaching the control it started on even when it wanders off.

terms.name: Preview text
terms.definition: The line an inbox prints under a subject, written as hidden text at the top of the mail so the client shows those words instead of scraping whatever body copy comes first.

terms.name: Pull quote
terms.definition: A phrase lifted out of an article and set large as a graphic element, to draw a browsing reader into the text.

terms.name: Rating prompt
terms.definition: An in-product request to rate or review, usually timed to a moment of success and often filtered so only positive responses reach the public store.

terms.name: Resize handle
terms.definition: The small corner grip that lets you drag an element or window bigger and smaller, drawn as diagonal ridges on a textarea or window corner.

terms.name: Route announcement
terms.definition: Telling assistive technology that a client side navigation happened, by moving focus to the new heading or posting the new title to a live region.

terms.name: Scrim
terms.definition: A translucent or gradient layer laid over imagery or behind a dialog, dimming what is beneath so text on top clears contrast or so focus moves forward.

terms.name: Secondary click
terms.definition: The alternate pointer press, usually the right button or a two-finger tap, reserved for opening contextual actions rather than activating.

terms.name: Shake
terms.definition: A short lateral wobble used to reject an input, borrowed from the head shake and read as no rather than as an error message.

terms.name: Slide transition
terms.definition: A transition where content translates in or out along one axis, using direction to say whether the user moved forward, back, up, or down.

terms.name: Sort state
terms.definition: The announced direction of the one column a table is currently sorted by, carried on that column header alone rather than on every sortable header.

terms.name: Spring loading
terms.definition: Hovering a dragged item over a container until it opens, so a drag can travel through nested destinations without being dropped and restarted.

terms.name: Sticky add to cart
terms.definition: A condensed product bar that pins itself to an edge once the real buy button has scrolled away, keeping price and purchase always reachable.

terms.name: Surface color
terms.definition: The colour of a plane that content sits on, defined as a set of stacked levels so a card on a page and a sheet on a card are told apart by value.

terms.name: Table of contents
terms.definition: A list of a document's sections, linked in reading order, shown beside or above the text.

terms.name: Three-way merge
terms.definition: Three versions on screen at once, mine, theirs, and the ancestor they both came from, with the result edited underneath so a conflict is decided rather than guessed.

terms.name: Toggletip
terms.definition: A tip revealed by clicking rather than hovering, so it works by touch and may contain links or controls a tooltip could not.

terms.name: True black theme
terms.definition: A dark palette whose background is pure black rather than near black, which switches OLED pixels off entirely but makes elements look like they float in a void.

terms.name: Use of color
terms.definition: The rule that colour must never be the only carrier of meaning, so a red field also needs an icon, wording, or shape change.

terms.name: Visual balance
terms.definition: The distribution of visual weight across a composition, reached by mirroring elements, by setting one large element against several small ones, or by radiating from a centre.

terms.name: Word break
terms.definition: Whether a long unbroken string is allowed to split mid-word rather than overflow its container, and where that split may happen.
